messages:
max: Heads-up: I sketched an experiment to combine an adaptive kernel selector with a pager-aware batching heuristic for paged-attn. Goal is to reduce tail latency when KV pages miss and avoid choosing large-kern kernels that thrash the pager.
anya: nice. can you paste the selector rules?
max: sure — simple rule set for now: 
```
# prioritized kernel list (higher first)
- fused_attn_small_seq: when seq<=512 and kv_hit_rate>0.6
- flash_sparse: when seq>512 and avg_page_faults_per_req<0.02
- fallback_stream: otherwise (low mem pressure)
```
Also a batching hint: prefer compact batches that share page prefixes; if page churn > 1.5x, reduce max batch size from 16 -> 6.
kevin: curious about the thresholds — how are you measuring kv_hit_rate and churn?
max: using recent per-request telemetry: kv_hit_rate = hits/(hits+misses) over 30s window. churn = moving_average(unique_pages_touched_per_second) / baseline_pages.
tariq: did you run microbenchmarks? any numbers?
anya: I ran a quick perf job on dev-gpu-3. results below (these are single-model, 4x3 token runs):
```
cfg: adaptive-selector ON, batch_hint=compact
requests: 1024 1-shot prompts
median p50_latency: 21.2ms
p95: 78.4ms
p99: 210.1ms
tokens/sec: 118k
page_fault_rate: 0.015
kv_hit_rate: 0.72
```
Compare baseline (static flash_sparse):
```
median p50_latency: 19.8ms
p95: 95.3ms
p99: 340.5ms
tokens/sec: 125k
page_fault_rate: 0.048
kv_hit_rate: 0.58
```
sophia: interesting — adaptive increases median slightly but tightens tail a lot. tokens/sec drop is expected with smaller batches when churn spikes.
kevin: the p99 improvement is compelling. but tokens/sec regression might hurt bursty workloads. can we have a cost knob to trade tail vs throughput?
max: yes plan is a tunable weight: alpha in [0,1] where score = alpha*tail_penalty + (1-alpha)*throughput_score. default alpha=0.7 for latency-sensitive customers.
tariq: any qual issues? do outputs change when switching kernels?
anya: ran diff checks on 500 eval prompts: identical tokens for fused_attn_small_seq vs flash_sparse in 98% of cases; remaining 2% are whitespace/float rounding diffs — acceptable for now.
pager-bot: nightly-regression-alert: paged-attn integration test suite failing on master, test: paged_attn_e2e_perf, delta p99 +120%
max: saw that alert. I dug into the trace — regression correlates with kernel-choice falling back to fallback_stream too often under mixed seq workloads. root cause looks like the kernel cost model got stale after the kernel refactor.
sophia: can we inject a quick patch: fall back to prefer flash_sparse when kv_hit_rate in [0.45,0.6] rather than immediate fallback_stream?
max: yes I'll open PR with that rule + a lightweight online calibration: for each kernel, maintain an exponential avg of observed latency per-seq-range and use that to rank kernels in real-time.
kevin: please also add a flag to run the new selector only on dedicated pools for first week. we don't want host customers hit by teething issues.
max: agreed. plan: 1) PR kernel selector + heuristic (A/B on dedicated), 2) run 24h microbench across seq mixes [128,512,2048], record p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec, 3) if p99 improves and avg tokens/sec not below -8% we roll to hosted.
tariq: can I own the microbench harness? I'll add page-pattern generators (prefix overlap, random churn, hotspot).
anya: I'll add a unit test for kernel-calibration that fakes latencies and ensures ranking converges.
sophia: also add telemetry tags: selector_version, reason_for_choice (kv_hit_based|latency_based|fallback). makes debugging easier.
max: thanks everyone. I'll open the PR shortly and post the bench command: 
```
./tools/bench_paged_attn --model smallpedia --seq-mix 128:40,512:40,2048:20 \
  --concurrency 32 --requests 2000 --page-pattern hotspot:70,random:30 \
  --selector=adaptive_v1 --emit-telemetry
```
kevin: looks good. after PR deploy, watch CBU and customer dashboards closely. ping me if p99 spikes. :eyes:
max: will do. closing loop here but will post PR link when ready.
